0.long_answer: Retinoschisin, also known as the X‐linked juvenile retinoschisis protein, is a lectin encoded by the RS1 gene located on the X chromosome at p22.1. The protein is secreted by retinal bipolar cells and photoreceptors, where it plays a key role in maintaining the structural integrity of the retina by binding to plasma membranes of retinal cells and facilitating cell-to-cell adhesion. Mutations in the RS1 gene lead to the genetic disorder X-linked retinoschisis, a condition that causes splitting of the retinal layers and subsequent vision loss, predominantly affecting young males.
